faults.name: Auxiliary input
faults.meaning: An external trip signal wired to a digital input set as Aux Fault has opened, so the drive stopped on purpose.
checks: Check the remote/external trip wiring and the device feeding that input
If the fault is not expected, review the digital input programming (t062, t063, t065-t068 set to 12 Aux Fault) and any comms-driven trip

faults.name: Power loss
faults.meaning: The drive saw a single-phase supply condition while carrying a heavy load.
checks: Look for low voltage or interruptions on the incoming AC supply
Check the input fuses
Reduce the load

faults.name: Undervoltage
faults.meaning: The DC bus fell below its minimum level, usually because the supply sagged or dropped out.
checks: Monitor the incoming AC line for low voltage or short interruptions

faults.name: Overvoltage
faults.meaning: The DC bus rose above its maximum level, from a high supply, line transients or motor regeneration.
checks: Monitor the AC line for high voltage or transients
If the motor regenerates, lengthen the decel time or fit a dynamic brake resistor option

faults.name: Motor stalled
faults.meaning: The drive could not accelerate or decelerate the motor, typically because it sat in current limit too long.
checks: Increase accel time (P041, A442, A444, A446) or reduce the load so output current stays below the current limit (A484, A485)
Check for an overhauling load

faults.name: Motor overload
faults.meaning: The internal electronic overload protection tripped because the motor drew excessive current for too long.
checks: Reduce the load so output current stays below the motor overload current (P033)
Verify the boost setting A530

faults.name: Heatsink overtemperature
faults.meaning: The heatsink/power module temperature exceeded its limit.
checks: Check for blocked or dirty heatsink fins and confirm ambient temperature is within rating
Check the cooling fan

faults.name: Control module overtemperature
faults.meaning: The control module temperature exceeded its limit.
checks: Check ambient temperature
Check for airflow obstruction
Check for dirt or debris
Check the fan

faults.name: Hardware overcurrent
faults.meaning: Drive output current exceeded the hardware current limit.
checks: Check programming
Check for excess load, wrong boost setting (A530), or DC brake voltage set too high, and other causes of excess current

faults.name: Ground fault
faults.meaning: A current path to earth was detected at one or more drive output terminals.
checks: Check the motor and external wiring from the output terminals for a grounded condition
faults.note: Type 1 fault that auto-restart may clear once, ignoring A541

faults.name: Load loss
faults.meaning: Output torque current stayed below the A490 level for longer than A491 time, so the load appears to be lost (e.g. broken belt or coupling).
checks: Verify the connection between motor and load
Verify the level (A490) and time (A491) settings

faults.name: Output phase loss
faults.meaning: Loss of an output phase was detected (only when the function is enabled with A557).
checks: Verify the motor wiring
Verify the motor

faults.name: Analog input loss
faults.meaning: An analog input configured to fault on signal loss has lost its signal.
checks: Check for broken or loose connections at the inputs
Check parameters t094 / t097 (signal-loss action)

faults.name: Auto restart tries exceeded
faults.meaning: The drive tried to reset a fault and resume running the number of times set in A541 and did not succeed.
checks: Correct the cause of the underlying fault and clear it manually

faults.name: Phase U to ground
faults.meaning: A ground fault was detected on motor phase U between the drive and the motor.
checks: Check the wiring between drive and motor
Check the motor for a grounded phase
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Phase V to ground
faults.meaning: A ground fault was detected on motor phase V between the drive and the motor.
checks: Check the wiring between drive and motor
Check the motor for a grounded phase
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Phase W to ground
faults.meaning: A ground fault was detected on motor phase W between the drive and the motor.
checks: Check the wiring between drive and motor
Check the motor for a grounded phase
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Phase UV short
faults.meaning: Excessive current was detected between two output terminals (UV), indicating a short.
checks: Check the motor and drive output terminal wiring for a short
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Phase UW short
faults.meaning: Excessive current was detected between two output terminals (UW), indicating a short.
checks: Check the motor and drive output terminal wiring for a short
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Phase VW short
faults.meaning: Excessive current was detected between two output terminals (VW), indicating a short.
checks: Check the motor and drive output terminal wiring for a short
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Parameters defaulted
faults.meaning: The drive was told to write factory default values to EEPROM.
checks: Clear the fault or cycle power
Re-program the drive parameters as needed

faults.name: Safety open
faults.meaning: Both safety inputs (Safety 1 and Safety 2) are de-energised, and t105 is set to fault in that state.
checks: Check the safety input signals
If safety is not used, verify and tighten the jumper across terminals S1, S2 and S+

faults.name: Software overcurrent (shear pin)
faults.meaning: Current stayed above the shear pin level (A486/A488) for longer than the shear pin time (A487/A489).
checks: Verify the connection between motor and load
Verify the level and time settings

faults.name: Drive overload
faults.meaning: The drive's own overload rating was exceeded.
checks: Reduce the load or extend the accel time

faults.name: Power unit
faults.meaning: A failure was detected in the drive power section.
checks: Check that the maximum ambient temperature has not been exceeded
Cycle power
Replace the drive if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: DSI network loss
faults.meaning: Control over the Modbus/DSI (RS-485) link was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the Modbus/DSI settings and status

faults.name: Option card network loss
faults.meaning: Control through the remote network of the optional network card was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the network adapter settings
Check the external network status

faults.name: Embedded EtherNet/IP network loss
faults.meaning: Control through the embedded EtherNet/IP adapter was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the EtherNet/IP settings
Check the external network status

faults.name: Autotune failure
faults.meaning: The autotune routine was cancelled by the user or did not complete successfully.
checks: Restart the procedure
Cycle power

faults.name: DSI communication loss
faults.meaning: Communication between the drive and the Modbus/DSI master was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the communications cabling
Check the Modbus/DSI settings and status
Modify the response with C125 (Comm Loss Action)
Connecting I/O terminals C1 and C2 to ground may improve noise immunity
Replace the wiring, Modbus master device or control module

faults.name: Option card communication loss
faults.meaning: Communication between the drive and the network option card was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Reinstall the option card in the drive
Modify the response with C125 (Comm Loss Action)
Replace the wiring, port expander, option card or control module

faults.name: Embedded EtherNet/IP communication loss
faults.meaning: Internal communication between the drive and the embedded EtherNet/IP adapter was interrupted.
checks: Cycle power
Check the EtherNet/IP settings
Check the drive's Ethernet settings and diagnostic parameters
Modify the response with C125 (Comm Loss Action)
Replace the wiring, Ethernet switch or control module

faults.name: Encoder loss
faults.meaning: One of the two encoder channel signals is missing (differential encoder required).
checks: Check the wiring
If P047/P049/P051 = 16 Positioning and A535 = 5 Quad Check, swap the encoder channel inputs or any two motor leads
Replace the encoder

faults.name: Function loss
faults.meaning: The Freeze-Fire (Function Loss) input is inactive, i.e. the input to the programmed terminal is open.
checks: Close the input to the terminal and cycle power

faults.name: Parameter checksum error
faults.meaning: The drive's non-volatile parameter storage is corrupted.
checks: Set P053 (Reset To Defaults) to 2 Factory Rset

faults.name: External storage error
faults.meaning: External non-volatile storage has failed.
checks: Set P053 (Reset To Defaults) to 2 Factory Rset

faults.name: Control module connect error
faults.meaning: The control module was disconnected while the drive was powered.
checks: Clear the fault and verify all parameter settings
Never remove or install the control module with power applied

faults.name: Incompatible control/power module
faults.meaning: The PowerFlex 525 control module does not support a power module with 0.25 HP rating.
checks: Change to a different power module
Change to a PowerFlex 523 control module

faults.name: Replaced control/power module
faults.meaning: The control module could not recognise the power module (hardware failure).
checks: Change to a different power module
Replace the control module if changing the power module does not help

faults.name: Control/power module mismatch
faults.meaning: The control module was mounted on a different drive type of power module.
checks: Set P053 (Reset To Defaults) to 3 Power Reset

faults.name: Keypad membrane
faults.meaning: The keypad membrane has failed or is disconnected.
checks: Cycle power
Replace the control module if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Safety hardware
faults.meaning: A malfunction in the safety input enable hardware; one of the safety inputs is not enabled.
checks: Cycle power
Check the safety input signals; if safety is not used, verify and tighten the jumper across terminals S1, S2 and S+
Verify the safety hardware; replace the control module if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Microprocessor failure
faults.meaning: Microprocessor failure.
checks: Cycle power
Verify grounding requirements (see General Grounding Requirements in the manual)
Replace the control module if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: I/O board failure
faults.meaning: A failure was detected in the drive control and I/O section.
checks: Cycle power
Replace the drive or control module if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: Flash update required
faults.meaning: The drive firmware is corrupt, mismatched or incompatible with the hardware.
checks: Perform a firmware flash update to load a valid set of firmware

faults.name: Non-recoverable error
faults.meaning: A non-recoverable firmware or hardware error was detected; the drive stopped and reset itself.
checks: Clear the fault or cycle power
Replace the drive or control module if the fault cannot be cleared

faults.name: DSI flash update required
faults.meaning: A critical firmware problem was detected and the drive is running backup firmware that supports only DSI communications.
checks: Perform a firmware flash update over DSI communications to load a valid set of firmware

params.name: Output Freq
params.desc: Live output frequency at the motor terminals, not including slip. First thing to look at when checking whether the drive is really running.

params.name: Commanded Freq
params.desc: The speed command the drive currently holds, shown even when stopped. If it is 0 while you expect a speed, the reference source is the problem.

params.name: Output Current
params.desc: Motor current in amps. Compare with P033 and the current limits when diagnosing overloads and stalls.

params.name: Output Voltage
params.desc: Voltage the drive is applying to the motor terminals.

params.name: DC Bus Voltage
params.desc: Filtered DC bus level. Useful for chasing F004 undervoltage and F005 overvoltage events.

params.name: Drive Status
params.desc: Bit-style readout of running, forward, accelerating, decelerating and (525) safety-active states.

params.name: Fault 1 Code
params.desc: Fault history entry; Fault 1 is the most recent. Repeated identical faults are logged once.

params.name: Fault 2 Code
params.desc: Older fault history entry (the lower the number, the more recent the fault).

params.name: Fault 3 Code
params.desc: Older fault history entry (the lower the number, the more recent the fault).

params.name: Process Display
params.desc: Output frequency scaled by A481 and A482 so the display can show a process value such as line speed.

params.name: Control Source
params.desc: Shows which source is currently supplying the start command and the frequency command. Check it first when the drive ignores your start or speed signals.

params.name: Contrl In Status
params.desc: Open/closed state of terminals 01-03 and the brake transistor, regardless of which source is actually in control.

params.name: Dig In Status
params.desc: Open/closed state of the programmable digital inputs (terminals 05-08; 07 and 08 only on the 525). Quick way to confirm field wiring.

params.name: Output RPM
params.desc: Output frequency converted to rpm using the pole count in P035.

params.name: Output Speed
params.desc: Output frequency as a percentage of P044.

params.name: Output Power
params.desc: Power being delivered to the motor, in kW.

params.name: Elapsed Run time
params.desc: Total hours the drive has been outputting power, counted in 10-hour steps.

params.name: Drive Temp
params.desc: Heatsink/power module temperature. Use when investigating F008.

params.name: Control Temp
params.desc: Control module temperature. Use when investigating F009.

params.name: Control SW Ver
params.desc: Firmware revision of the drive; note it when asking for support or checking which parameters your unit has.

params.name: Language
params.range: 1 to 15 (1 English, 2 Francais, 3 Espanol, 4 Italiano, 5 Deutsch, 6 Japanese, 7 Portugues, 8 Chinese, 11 Korean, 12 Polish, 14 Turkish, 15 Czech)
params.desc: Display language. Needs a reset or power cycle to take effect; not touched by parameter reset.

params.name: Motor NP Volts
params.desc: Motor nameplate voltage. Drive must be stopped to change it; the V/Hz curve is built from it.

params.name: Motor NP Hertz
params.desc: Motor nameplate frequency (base frequency). Set it to 50 Hz for typical European motors.

params.name: Motor OL Current
params.desc: Overload current reference for the electronic motor thermal model (set to the nameplate amps). The drive trips F007 when this is exceeded long enough.

params.name: Motor NP FLA
params.desc: Motor full-load amps from the nameplate; used by autotune and motor control.

params.name: Motor NP Poles
params.desc: Number of motor poles; used to display rpm.

params.name: Motor NP RPM
params.desc: Nameplate rpm, from which rated slip is worked out. Enter it accurately; if the motor runs at the wrong speed, check this and P032.

params.name: Motor NP Power
params.desc: Motor nameplate power, used by the permanent-magnet motor regulator (525 only).

params.name: Voltage Class
params.desc: Selects the voltage class on 600V drives. Stop the drive before changing.

params.name: Torque Perf Mode
params.range: 0 V/Hz, 1 SVC, 2 Economize, 3 Vector, 4 PM Control, 5 SynRM
params.desc: Motor control mode. V/Hz is the simple fallback; Vector, PM and SynRM modes are 525-only and depend on firmware level.

params.name: Autotune
params.desc: Runs a motor measurement routine after you give a start command. Enter all motor data first; static tune measures stator resistance, rotate tune also measures flux current and should be done with the load uncoupled. Failure gives F080.

params.name: Accel Time 1
params.desc: Seconds to ramp from 0 Hz to Maximum Freq. Lengthen if the drive hits current limit or trips on acceleration.

params.name: Decel Time 1
params.desc: Seconds to ramp from Maximum Freq to 0 Hz. Lengthen to avoid F005 overvoltage from regeneration.

params.name: Minimum Freq
params.desc: Lowest frequency the drive will output while running.

params.name: Maximum Freq
params.desc: Highest output frequency; also the reference for accel/decel rates. Must be above Minimum Freq.

params.name: Stop Mode
params.range: 0 Ramp CF, 1 Coast CF, 2 DC Brake CF, 3 DC BrkAuto CF, 4 Ramp, 5 Coast, 6 DC Brake, 7 DC BrakeAuto, 8 Ramp+EM B CF, 9 Ramp+EM Brk, 10 PointStp CF, 11 PointStop
params.desc: How the drive stops. Options marked CF also let the Stop key clear a fault; EM-brake and PointStop variants are for brake and fixed-distance stopping.

params.name: Start Source 1
params.range: 1 Keypad, 2 DigIn TrmBlk, 3 Serial/DSI, 4 Network Opt, 5 EtherNet/IP
params.desc: Primary source of the Run command. If the drive does not start from the terminals, this is the first setting to check.

params.name: Speed Reference1
params.range: 1 Drive Pot, 2 Keypad Freq, 3 Serial/DSI, 4 Network Opt, 5 0-10V Input, 6 4-20mA Input, 7 Preset Freq, 8 Anlg In Mult, 9 MOP, 10 Pulse Input, 11 PID1 Output, 12 PID2 Output, 13 Step Logic, 14 Encoder, 15 EtherNet/IP, 16 Positioning
params.desc: Primary source of the speed command (several options are 525-only).

params.name: Start Source 2
params.range: 1 Keypad, 2 DigIn TrmBlk, 3 Serial/DSI, 4 Network Opt, 5 EtherNet/IP
params.desc: Alternate start source, selected by a digital input.

params.name: Speed Reference2
params.desc: Alternate speed reference, selected by a digital input.

params.name: Start Source 3
params.range: 1 Keypad, 2 DigIn TrmBlk, 3 Serial/DSI, 4 Network Opt, 5 EtherNet/IP
params.desc: Third start source, normally the communications source.

params.name: Speed Reference3
params.desc: Third speed reference, normally the communications source.

params.name: Average kWh Cost
params.desc: Energy price per kWh used for the cost-savings readout.

params.name: Reset To Defalts
params.range: 0 Ready/Idle, 1 Param Reset, 2 Factory Rset, 3 Power Reset, 4 Module Reset
params.desc: Restores parameters. 1 keeps language, custom group and comms settings; 2 is a full factory reset; 3 resets only power-related parameters (use after swapping power modules); 4 just power-cycles. Stop the drive first.

params.name: Display Param
params.desc: Chooses what the display shows at power-up.

params.name: DigIn TermBlk 02
params.range: 0 to 52 (0 Not Used, 1 Speed Ref 2, 2 Speed Ref 3, 3 Start Src 2, 4 Start Src 3, 5 Spd+Strt 2, 6 Spd+Strt 3, 7 Preset Freq, 8 Jog, 9 Jog Forward, 10 Jog Reverse, 11 Acc/Dec Sel2, 12 Aux Fault, 13 Clear Fault, 14 RampStop CF, 15 CoastStop CF, 16 DCInjStop CF, 17 MOP Up, 18 MOP Down, 19 Timer Start, 20 Counter In, 21 Reset Timer, 22 Reset Countr, 23 Rset Tim&Cnt, 24 Logic In 1, 25 Logic In 2, 26 Current Lmt2, 27 Anlg Invert, 28 EM Brk Rlse, 29 Acc/Dec Sel3, 30 Precharge En, 31 Inertia Dcel, 32 Sync Enable, 33 Traverse Dis, 34 Home Limit, 35 Find Home, 36 Hold Step, 37 Pos Redefine, 38 Force DC, 39 Damper Input, 40 Purge, 41 Freeze-Fire, 42 SW Enable, 43 SherPin1 Dis; 48 and 49 apply to this terminal only)
params.desc: Function of terminal 02. Default is run forward in 2-wire mode; choose 3-Wire Start for a start/stop pushbutton arrangement.

params.name: DigIn TermBlk 03
params.range: 0 to 52 (50 2-Wire REV and 51 3-Wire Dir apply to this terminal only; otherwise as t062)
params.desc: Function of terminal 03. Default is run reverse in 2-wire mode.

params.name: DigIn TermBlk 05
params.desc: Function of terminal 05; defaults to a preset-frequency select input.

params.name: DigIn TermBlk 06
params.desc: Function of terminal 06; defaults to a preset-frequency select input.

params.name: DigIn TermBlk 07
params.desc: Function of terminal 07 (PowerFlex 525 only). Also the pulse-train input terminal on the 525.

params.name: DigIn TermBlk 08
params.desc: Function of terminal 08 (PowerFlex 525 only).

params.name: 2-Wire Mode
params.range: 0 Edge Trigger, 1 Level Sense, 2 Hi-Spd Edge, 3 Momentary
params.desc: How 2-wire run inputs behave. Level Sense lets the drive restart as soon as stop is released while run is still held, so use it with care.

params.name: Opto Out1 Sel
params.range: 0 to 31 (0 Ready/Fault, 1 At Frequency, 2 MotorRunning, 3 Reverse, 4 Motor Overld, 5 Ramp Reg, 6 Above Freq, 7 Above Cur, 8 Above DCVolt, 9 Retries Exst, 10 Above Anlg V, 11 Above PF Ang, 12 Anlg In Loss, 13 ParamControl, 14 NonRec Fault, 15 EM Brk Cntrl, 16 Thermal OL, 17 Amb OverTemp, 18 Local Active, 19 Comm Loss, 20-24 logic/StepLogic, 25 Timer Out, 26 Counter Out, 27 At Position, 28 At Home, 29 Safe-Off, 30 SafeTqPermit, 31 AutoRst Ctdn)
params.desc: Condition that switches optocoupler output 1 (PowerFlex 525 only).

params.name: Opto Out2 Sel
params.desc: Condition that switches optocoupler output 2 (PowerFlex 525 only).

params.name: Opto Out1 Level
params.desc: Threshold for opto output 1 when the selected function compares against a level (frequency, current %, voltage, etc.).

params.name: Opto Out2 Level
params.desc: Threshold for opto output 2 when its function uses a level.

params.name: Opto Out Logic
params.desc: Sets whether each opto output acts normally open or normally closed.

params.name: Relay Out1 Sel
params.desc: Condition that switches relay 1 (terminals R1, R2, R3). Default signals ready/fault, handy as a fault contact to a PLC.

params.name: Relay Out2 Sel
params.desc: Condition that switches relay 2 (PowerFlex 525 only).

params.name: Relay Out1 Level
params.desc: Threshold for relay 1 when its function compares against a level.

params.name: Relay Out2 Level
params.desc: Threshold for relay 2 when its function uses a level.

params.name: Relay 1 On Time
params.desc: Delay before relay 1 energises after its condition is met.

params.name: Relay 1 Off Time
params.desc: Delay before relay 1 de-energises after its condition clears.

params.name: EM Brk Off Delay
params.desc: With EM brake stop mode, time the drive holds minimum frequency after the brake is released before ramping up.

params.name: EM Brk On Delay
params.desc: With EM brake stop mode, time the drive holds minimum frequency before the brake is applied at stop.

params.name: Analog Out Sel
params.range: 0 to 23 (0-10V, 0-20mA and 4-20mA ranges for frequency, current, voltage, power, torque, test data, setpoint, DC bus)
params.desc: Chooses what the analog output signal represents and its electrical range.

params.name: Analog Out High
params.desc: Scales the analog output at full-scale source value.

params.name: Anlg Out Setpt
params.desc: Fixed output level used when the analog output is set to a setpoint option; handy for testing a meter or PLC input.

params.name: Anlg In 0-10V Lo
params.desc: Percentage of 10V that corresponds to Minimum Freq. Set above t092 to invert the input.

params.name: Anlg In 0-10V Hi
params.desc: Percentage of 10V that corresponds to Maximum Freq.

params.name: 10V Bipolar Enbl
params.desc: Enables +/-10V input where the voltage polarity sets direction (525 only).

params.name: Anlg In V Loss
params.range: 0 Disabled, 1 Fault (F29), 2 Stop, 3 Zero Ref, 4 Min Freq Ref, 5 Max Freq Ref, 6 Key Freq Ref, 7 MOP Freq Ref, 8 Continu Last
params.desc: What to do when the 0-10V signal drops below 1V. Choose Fault to get F029.

params.name: Anlg In4-20mA Lo
params.desc: Percentage of the 4-20 mA range that corresponds to Minimum Freq.

params.name: Anlg In4-20mA Hi
params.desc: Percentage of the 4-20 mA range that corresponds to Maximum Freq.

params.name: Anlg In mA Loss
params.range: 0 Disabled, 1 Fault (F29), 2 Stop, 3 Zero Ref, 4 Min Freq Ref, 5 Max Freq Ref, 6 Key Freq Ref, 7 MOP Freq Ref, 8 Continu Last
params.desc: What to do when the 4-20 mA signal falls below 2 mA (broken-loop detection).

params.name: Anlg Loss Delay
params.desc: Grace period after power-up during which signal loss is ignored.

params.name: Analog In Filter
params.desc: Extra filtering on analog inputs; each step roughly doubles the filtering and slows response.

params.name: Sleep-Wake Sel
params.desc: Enables sleep mode, which ramps the drive to zero when the chosen signal stays low, and wakes it again. Can cause unexpected starts.

params.name: Sleep Level
params.desc: Signal level below which the drive goes to sleep.

params.name: Sleep Time
params.desc: How long the signal must stay below the sleep level before sleeping.

params.name: Wake Level
params.desc: Signal level above which the drive wakes.

params.name: Wake Time
params.desc: How long the signal must stay above the wake level before waking.

params.name: Safety Open En
params.desc: Whether the drive faults (F059) when both safety inputs are de-energised (525 only).

params.name: SafetyFlt RstCfg
params.desc: Whether F111 needs a power cycle or can be cleared with a normal fault reset (525, newer firmware).

params.name: Comm Write Mode
params.desc: Whether values written over comms go to permanent memory or only RAM. Keep at Save if Automatic Drive Configuration is used.

params.name: Cmd Stat Select
params.desc: Chooses the velocity or position bit layout of the network command/status words (525 only).

params.name: RS485 Data Rate
params.desc: Baud rate for the RS-485 (Modbus/DSI) port. Takes effect after reset or power cycle.

params.name: RS485 Node Addr
params.desc: Modbus slave address of the drive on the RS-485 port. Takes effect after reset or power cycle.

params.name: Comm Loss Action
params.range: 0 Fault, 1 Coast Stop, 2 Stop, 3 Continu Last
params.desc: Response to lost RS-485 communication. Fault gives F081; Continue Last keeps running at the last speed, so use with care.

params.name: Comm Loss Time
params.desc: How long RS-485 communication may be lost before the C125 action is taken.

params.name: RS485 Format
params.range: 0 RTU 8-N-1, 1 RTU 8-E-1, 2 RTU 8-O-1, 3 RTU 8-N-2, 4 RTU 8-E-2, 5 RTU 8-O-2
params.desc: Modbus RTU data bits/parity/stop bits. Must match the master; reset or power cycle needed.

params.name: EN Addr Sel
params.desc: Selects whether the embedded Ethernet address comes from the C129-C140 parameters or a BOOTP server. Set to 1 to use fixed addresses. Reset or power cycle needed.

params.name: EN IP Addr Cfg 1
params.default: 0 (byte 1 of the IP address; manual's example shows 192.168.1.62)
params.desc: Byte 1 of the static IP address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN IP Addr Cfg 2
params.default: 0 (byte 2 of the IP address; manual's example shows 192.168.1.62)
params.desc: Byte 2 of the static IP address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN IP Addr Cfg 3
params.default: 0 (byte 3 of the IP address; manual's example shows 192.168.1.62)
params.desc: Byte 3 of the static IP address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN IP Addr Cfg 4
params.default: 0 (byte 4 of the IP address; manual's example shows 192.168.1.62)
params.desc: Byte 4 of the static IP address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Subnet Cfg 1
params.default: 0 (byte 1 of the subnet mask; manual's example shows 255.255.255.0)
params.desc: Byte 1 of the subnet mask; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Subnet Cfg 2
params.default: 0 (byte 2 of the subnet mask; manual's example shows 255.255.255.0)
params.desc: Byte 2 of the subnet mask; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Subnet Cfg 3
params.default: 0 (byte 3 of the subnet mask; manual's example shows 255.255.255.0)
params.desc: Byte 3 of the subnet mask; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Subnet Cfg 4
params.default: 0 (byte 4 of the subnet mask; manual's example shows 255.255.255.0)
params.desc: Byte 4 of the subnet mask; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Gateway Cfg 1
params.default: 0 (byte 1 of the gateway; manual's example shows 192.168.1.1)
params.desc: Byte 1 of the gateway address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Gateway Cfg 2
params.default: 0 (byte 2 of the gateway; manual's example shows 192.168.1.1)
params.desc: Byte 2 of the gateway address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Gateway Cfg 3
params.default: 0 (byte 3 of the gateway; manual's example shows 192.168.1.1)
params.desc: Byte 3 of the gateway address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Gateway Cfg 4
params.default: 0 (byte 4 of the gateway; manual's example shows 192.168.1.1)
params.desc: Byte 4 of the gateway address; used only when C128 = Parameters.

params.name: EN Rate Cfg
params.range: 0 Auto detect, 1 10Mbps Full, 2 10Mbps Half, 3 100Mbps Full, 4 100Mbps Half
params.desc: Ethernet speed/duplex for the embedded port. Leave on auto unless the switch port is hard-set. Needs reset or power cycle.

params.name: EN Comm Flt Actn
params.range: 0 Fault, 1 Stop, 2 Zero Data, 3 Hold Last, 4 Send Flt Cfg
params.desc: What the drive does if EtherNet/IP communication is lost. Fault gives F073/F083; other options keep the drive running, so verify safe behaviour at commissioning.

params.name: EN Idle Flt Actn
params.range: 0 Fault, 1 Stop, 2 Zero Data, 3 Hold Last, 4 Send Flt Cfg
params.desc: What the drive does when the PLC goes to program mode (scanner idle). Same options as C143.

params.name: EN Flt Cfg Logic
params.desc: Logic command word sent to the drive when C143 or C144 is Send Flt Cfg.

params.name: EN Flt Cfg Ref
params.desc: Speed reference sent to the drive when C143 or C144 is Send Flt Cfg.

params.name: EN Flt Cfg DL 1
params.desc: Datalink 1 value sent to the drive on a fault-configured communication fault or idle.

params.name: EN Flt Cfg DL 2
params.desc: Datalink 2 value sent to the drive on a fault-configured communication fault or idle.

params.name: EN Flt Cfg DL 3
params.desc: Datalink 3 value sent to the drive on a fault-configured communication fault or idle.

params.name: EN Flt Cfg DL 4
params.desc: Datalink 4 value sent to the drive on a fault-configured communication fault or idle.

params.name: EN Data In 1
params.desc: Parameter number written by EtherNet/IP Datalink input 1 from the PLC. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data In 2
params.desc: Parameter number written by EtherNet/IP Datalink input 2 from the PLC. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data In 3
params.desc: Parameter number written by EtherNet/IP Datalink input 3 from the PLC. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data In 4
params.desc: Parameter number written by EtherNet/IP Datalink input 4 from the PLC. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data Out 1
params.desc: Parameter number read back to the PLC through EtherNet/IP Datalink output 1. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data Out 2
params.desc: Parameter number read back to the PLC through EtherNet/IP Datalink output 2. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data Out 3
params.desc: Parameter number read back to the PLC through EtherNet/IP Datalink output 3. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: EN Data Out 4
params.desc: Parameter number read back to the PLC through EtherNet/IP Datalink output 4. Cannot be changed while an I/O connection is open.

params.name: MultiDrv Sel
params.desc: Enables multi-drive mode, with this drive as master and up to four slaves daisy-chained on RS-485. Reset or power cycle needed.

params.name: DSI I/O Cfg
params.desc: Which drives take part in the multi-drive set-up.

params.name: Analog In 0-10V
params.desc: Live 0-10V analog input as a percentage; compare with a meter to verify the signal.

params.name: Analog In 4-20mA
params.desc: Live 4-20 mA analog input as a percentage.

params.name: Elapsed Time-hr
params.desc: Run-time hours counter, resettable via A555.

params.name: Counter Status
params.desc: Count accumulated by the internal counter function.

params.name: Motor OL Level
params.desc: How full the motor thermal overload counter is; at 100% an F007 trip is imminent.

params.name: Slip Hz Meter
params.desc: Present slip compensation applied.

params.name: Torque Current
params.desc: Torque-producing portion of motor current.

params.name: Dig Out Status
params.desc: State of relay and opto outputs; check it to confirm what the drive is commanding to a PLC.

params.name: Preset Freq 0
params.desc: Fixed speed 0 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 1
params.desc: Fixed speed 1 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 2
params.desc: Fixed speed 2 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 3
params.desc: Fixed speed 3 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 4
params.desc: Fixed speed 4 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 5
params.desc: Fixed speed 5 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 6
params.desc: Fixed speed 6 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 7
params.desc: Fixed speed 7 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 8
params.desc: Fixed speed 8 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 9
params.desc: Fixed speed 9 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 10
params.desc: Fixed speed 10 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 11
params.desc: Fixed speed 11 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 12
params.desc: Fixed speed 12 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 13
params.desc: Fixed speed 13 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 14
params.desc: Fixed speed 14 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Preset Freq 15
params.desc: Fixed speed 15 selected by the preset-frequency digital inputs. Preset 0 is only used if a speed reference is set to Preset Freq.

params.name: Keypad Freq
params.desc: Speed command used when a speed reference is set to Keypad Freq; also changed with the keypad arrows.

params.name: MOP Freq
params.desc: Speed command held by the motor-operated-potentiometer function (MOP up/down inputs).

params.name: MOP Reset Sel
params.range: 0 Zero MOP Ref, 1 Save MOP Ref
params.desc: Whether the MOP frequency is kept or zeroed at power-down.

params.name: MOP Time
params.desc: How fast the MOP speed changes while up/down is held.

params.name: Jog Frequency
params.desc: Speed used for jog commands.

params.name: Jog Accel/Decel
params.desc: Ramp time used while jogging.

params.name: Purge Frequency
params.desc: Fixed speed used by the Purge digital input function.

params.name: DC Brake Time
params.desc: Duration of DC injection braking at stop.

params.name: DC Brake Level
params.desc: DC braking current. Do not use with synchronous motors; mechanical brake needed where a hazard exists.

params.name: DC Brk Time@Strt
params.desc: DC current applied for this long after a start command, before ramping (pre-magnetise or hold).

params.name: DB Resistor Sel
params.range: 0 Disabled, 1 Norml RA Res, 2 NoProtection, 3-99 duty cycle %
params.desc: Enables an external dynamic-brake resistor and sets the protection level. When on, the bus regulator A550 is ignored.

params.name: DB Threshold
params.desc: DC bus level at which the brake resistor switches in. Values below about 90% are rarely needed and can overheat the resistor.

params.name: S Curve %
params.desc: Rounds the start and end of accel/decel ramps for smoother motion.

params.name: PWM Frequency
params.desc: Carrier frequency. Higher is quieter but derates output current.

params.name: Droop Hertz@ FLA
params.desc: Reduces output frequency in proportion to load for load sharing (525 only).

params.name: Accel Time 2
params.desc: Alternate accel ramp, selected via digital input.

params.name: Decel Time 2
params.desc: Alternate decel ramp, selected via digital input.

params.name: Accel Time 3
params.desc: Third accel ramp, selectable by digital inputs.

params.name: Decel Time 3
params.desc: Third decel ramp, selectable by digital inputs.

params.name: Accel Time 4
params.desc: Fourth accel ramp, selectable by digital inputs.

params.name: Decel Time 4
params.desc: Fourth decel ramp, selectable by digital inputs.

params.name: Skip Frequency 1
params.desc: Centre of a speed range to avoid, e.g. to dodge a mechanical resonance (525 only).

params.name: Skip Freq Band 1
params.desc: Width of the avoided range around skip frequency 1.

params.name: Skip Frequency 2
params.desc: Centre of a speed range to avoid, e.g. to dodge a mechanical resonance (525 only).

params.name: Skip Freq Band 2
params.desc: Width of the avoided range around skip frequency 2.

params.name: Skip Frequency 3
params.desc: Centre of a speed range to avoid, e.g. to dodge a mechanical resonance (525 only).

params.name: Skip Freq Band 3
params.desc: Width of the avoided range around skip frequency 3.

params.name: Skip Frequency 4
params.desc: Centre of a speed range to avoid, e.g. to dodge a mechanical resonance (525 only).

params.name: Skip Freq Band 4
params.desc: Width of the avoided range around skip frequency 4.

params.name: PID 1 Trim Sel
params.desc: Applies PID1 output as a trim on top of the chosen speed reference (525 only).

params.name: PID 1 Ref Sel
params.desc: Source of the PID1 reference (525 only).

params.name: PID 1 Fdback Sel
params.range: 0 0-10V Input, 1 4-20mA Input, 2 Serial/DSI, 3 Network Opt, 4 Pulse Input, 5 Encoder, 6 EtherNet/IP
params.desc: Source of the PID1 feedback signal (525 only).

params.name: PID 1 Prop Gain
params.desc: Proportional gain of PID1.

params.name: PID 1 Integ Time
params.desc: Integral time of PID1.

params.name: PID 1 Diff Rate
params.desc: Differential rate of PID1 (1/s).

params.name: PID 1 Setpoint
params.desc: Internal fixed setpoint for PID1.

params.name: PID 1 Deadband
params.desc: Error band around the reference that PID1 ignores.

params.name: PID 1 Invert Err
params.desc: Flips the PID1 error sign for reverse-acting processes.

params.name: Process Disp Lo
params.desc: Value shown in b010 at minimum frequency.

params.name: Process Disp Hi
params.desc: Value shown in b010 at maximum frequency.

params.name: Current Limit 1
params.range: 0.0 to Drive Rated Amps x 1.5 (Normal Duty) or x 1.8 (Heavy Duty)
params.default: Drive Rated Amps x 1.1 (Normal Duty); x 1.5 (Heavy Duty)
params.desc: Maximum output current before the drive reduces speed/torque. Lower it to protect the load; too low causes stall (F006).

params.name: Current Limit 2
params.range: 0.0 to Drive Rated Amps x 1.5 (Normal Duty) or x 1.8 (Heavy Duty)
params.desc: Second current limit, activated by a digital input (525 only).

params.name: Shear Pin1 Level
params.desc: Current level that triggers shear-pin fault 1 if sustained (525 only).

params.name: Shear Pin 1 Time
params.desc: How long current must exceed A486 before F063 (525 only).

params.name: Shear Pin2 Level
params.desc: Current level for shear-pin fault 2 (525 only).

params.name: Shear Pin 2 Time
params.desc: How long current must exceed A488 before F063 (525 only).

params.name: Load Loss Level
params.desc: Current below which the load is considered lost (F015); 0 leaves it off (525 only).

params.name: Load Loss Time
params.desc: How long current must stay under A490 before F015 (525 only).

params.name: Stall Fault Time
params.desc: How long the drive may stay stalled before F006 is raised.

params.name: Motor OL Select
params.range: 0 No Derate, 1 Min Derate, 2 Max Derate
params.desc: Whether the Class 10 overload curve is derated at low speed, for self-cooled motors.

params.name: Motor OL Ret
params.desc: Whether the motor overload counter is kept through power-off or cleared at power-up.

params.name: Drive OL Mode
params.range: 0 Disabled, 1 Reduce CLim, 2 Reduce PWM, 3 Both-PWM 1st
params.desc: How the drive protects itself from overload before faulting (F064): lower the current limit, lower the carrier frequency, or both.

params.name: IR Voltage Drop
params.desc: Voltage dropped across the motor stator resistance; set by autotune.

params.name: Flux Current Ref
params.desc: Current needed for full motor flux (roughly the no-load current); set by rotate tune.

params.name: Boost Select
params.default: 6 (2.5 CT) for 400/600V 5 HP and above; 7 (2.5 CT) for 200V 5 HP and above; 8 (5.0 CT) for drives below 5 HP
params.desc: Chooses the V/Hz curve and low-speed voltage boost (VT for fans/pumps, CT for constant-torque loads). Used in V/Hz control. Too much boost causes overcurrent or overload faults; too little gives poor starting.

params.name: Start Boost
params.desc: Low-frequency voltage boost when A530 is Custom V/Hz.

params.name: Break Voltage
params.desc: Voltage at the break frequency on a custom V/Hz curve.

params.name: Break Frequency
params.desc: Frequency at which the break voltage is applied on a custom curve.

params.name: Maximum Voltage
params.desc: Highest voltage the drive will output.

params.name: Motor Fdbk Type
params.range: 0 None, 1 Pulse Train, 2 Single Chan, 3 Single Check, 4 Quadrature, 5 Quad Check
params.desc: Type of speed feedback used. Quadrature types need the optional encoder card (525).

params.name: Encoder PPR
params.desc: Encoder pulses per revolution (525 only).

params.name: Pulse In Scale
params.desc: Scaling for pulse-train input: input Hz divided by this value gives output Hz.

params.name: Ki Speed Loop
params.desc: Integral gain of the closed-loop speed regulator.

params.name: Kp Speed Loop
params.desc: Proportional gain of the closed-loop speed regulator.

params.name: Var PWM Disable
params.desc: Allows or blocks automatic lowering of carrier frequency at low speed.

params.name: Auto Rstrt Tries
params.desc: How many times the drive retries after a resettable fault. Leave 0 unless automatic restart is safe for the machine.

params.name: Auto Rstrt Delay
params.desc: Wait between automatic restart attempts. Setting 0 with tries above 0 clears overvoltage/undervoltage/heatsink faults without restarting.

params.name: Start At PowerUp
params.desc: Allows the drive to start on power-up if a run signal is already present. Hazardous if unintended.

params.name: Reverse Disable
params.desc: Blocks reverse rotation when set to 1. Check this if the drive refuses to run in reverse.

params.name: Flying Start En
params.desc: Lets the drive catch a motor that is already spinning and ramp from its actual speed.

params.name: FlyStrt CurLimit
params.desc: Current level used to decide the drive has locked on to the spinning motor.

params.name: Compensation
params.desc: Corrections for motor instability or resonance; try it when the motor hunts.

params.name: Power Loss Mode
params.desc: Reaction to loss of input power: coast with a fault, or decelerate to hold up the DC bus.

params.name: Half Bus Enable
params.desc: Ride-through for short supply dips at half voltage; needs enough line impedance.

params.name: Bus Reg Enable
params.desc: Bus regulator that stretches decel time to avoid overvoltage. Disable when using a brake resistor or PointStop.

params.name: Fault Clear
params.desc: Clears the active fault, and with 2 also empties the fault history.

params.name: Program Lock
params.desc: Four-digit code protecting parameters from changes.

params.name: Program Lock Mod
params.range: 0 Full Lock, 1 Keypad Lock, 2 Custom Only, 3 KeyPd Custom
params.desc: How the lock in A552 behaves (all parameters, keypad only, or custom group access).

params.name: Drv Ambient Sel
params.desc: Declares the expected ambient above 50 C so the drive derates properly.

params.name: Reset Meters
params.desc: Clears energy meters or run-time counters.

params.name: Out Phas Loss En
params.desc: Turns on output phase-loss detection (F021).

params.name: Speed Ratio
params.desc: Scales the speed command.

params.name: Mtr Options Cfg
params.desc: Enables jerk limiting and zero-speed slip suppression options.

params.name: RdyBit Mode Cfg
params.desc: Selects which stop conditions drop the network Ready bit. Reset or power cycle needed.

params.name: Flux Braking En
params.desc: Enables flux braking for faster stops without a resistor.

params.name: Fault 4 Code
params.desc: Fault history slot 4 (F604 to F610 hold slots 4 to 10).

params.name: Fault 1 Time-hr
params.desc: Run-time hour count when fault 1 occurred (525 only; slots 2-10 follow).

params.name: Fault 1 Freq
params.desc: Output frequency when fault 1 occurred (525 only).

params.name: Fault 1 Current
params.desc: Output current when fault 1 occurred. Useful for telling overload from short.

params.name: Fault 1 BusVolts
params.desc: DC bus voltage when fault 1 occurred.

params.name: Status @ Fault 1
params.desc: Drive status bits at the moment of fault 1 (525 only).

params.name: Comm Sts - DSI
params.desc: Status of the RS-485 port: Rx, Tx, connection type and error digits.

params.name: Comm Sts - Opt
params.desc: Status of the internal communication option.

params.name: Com Sts-Emb Enet
params.desc: Status of the embedded EtherNet/IP port (525 only).

params.name: EN Addr Src
params.desc: Shows whether the Ethernet address came from parameters or BOOTP.

params.name: EN Rate Act
params.range: 0 No Link, 1 10Mbps Full, 2 10Mbps Half, 3 100Mbps Full, 4 100Mbps Half, 5 Dup IP Addr, 6 Disabled
params.desc: Actual Ethernet link state; No Link means a cable/switch problem and Dup IP Addr flags an address conflict.

params.name: HW Addr 1
params.desc: First byte of the MAC address (F687-F692 hold all six bytes).

params.name: EN IP Addr Act 1
params.desc: First byte of the IP address in use (F693-F696 hold the four bytes; 0 if none).

params.name: EN Subnet Act 1
params.desc: First byte of the subnet mask in use (F697-F700).

params.name: EN Gateway Act 1
params.desc: First byte of the gateway in use (F701-F704).

params.name: EN Rx Overruns
params.desc: Count of received-packet overruns on the Ethernet port; rising values suggest network trouble.

params.name: EN Rx Errors
params.desc: Count of Ethernet receive errors.

params.name: EN Tx Errors
params.desc: Count of Ethernet transmit errors.

params.name: EN Missed IO Pkt
params.desc: Count of missed I/O packets, a sign of an unreliable EtherNet/IP connection.

params.name: DSI Errors
params.desc: Count of RS-485 (DSI/Modbus) communication errors.
